mnemonic.meaning: YAGATE: "YA, GATE's opening soon!" Before long, it happens.

examples.ja: やがて雨が止んで、空が明るくなった。
examples.en: Before long the rain stopped and the sky got brighter.

items.note: Written and story-like. Narrates something that happens after a while.

mnemonic.meaning: FUTO: a puff ("fu") of an idea that pops in out of nowhere.

examples.ja: ふと昔のことを思い出した。
examples.en: I suddenly remembered the old days.

items.note: For thoughts or actions that happen without planning: ふと思う, ふと見る. Not for loud sudden events (that's 突然).

mnemonic.meaning: SOTTO: say it softly, "sotto voce". Gently, without a sound.

examples.ja: 赤ちゃんが寝ているので、そっとドアを閉めた。
examples.en: The baby was sleeping, so I closed the door quietly.

items.note: そっとしておく = leave someone alone.

mnemonic.meaning: JITTO: stay "jit" still, like a jittery cat frozen in place.

examples.ja: 猫が窓の外をじっと見ている。
examples.en: The cat is staring out of the window.

items.note: じっと見る = to stare. じっとする = to keep still.

mnemonic.meaning: 肌 has 月 (body part): the part of the body on the outside. Skin.
mnemonic.reading: HADA: "HA! DA-ry skin!" (はだ)

examples.ja: 冬は肌が乾燥しやすい。
examples.en: Skin gets dry easily in winter.

items.note: 皮膚 (ひふ) is the medical word. 肌 is everyday, also for texture and feel.

mnemonic.meaning: 頬 has 頁 (head): a part of the face. The cheek.
mnemonic.reading: HOHO: you go "ho ho" and your cheeks puff up. (ほほ) Also read ほお.

examples.ja: 恥ずかしくて頬が赤くなった。
examples.en: My cheeks turned red with embarrassment.

items.note: Both ほほ and ほお are correct.

mnemonic.meaning: 鋭 has 金 (metal): a sharp metal blade.
mnemonic.reading: "SURU-DOI!" The knife slides through (する) like a doorknob (ドア). (するどい)

examples.ja: このナイフはとても鋭い。
examples.en: This knife is very sharp.

items.note: Also for minds and eyes: 鋭い質問 (a sharp question). 鈍い (にぶい) is the opposite.

mnemonic.meaning: ARU (there is) + IWA: there is this, or that.

examples.ja: 電話、あるいはメールで連絡してください。
examples.en: Please contact us by phone or email.

items.note: Formal version of または / か. Also "perhaps": あるいは本当かもしれない.

mnemonic.meaning: 互 means mutual: two hooks holding each other.
mnemonic.reading: "Oh, TAGAI!" You both say it to each other. (おたがい)

examples.ja: お互いに助け合いましょう。
examples.en: Let's help each other.

items.note: お互い様 = "we're in the same boat", said when both sides owe each other.

mnemonic.meaning: 馬 horse + 鹿 deer: someone who can't tell a horse from a deer. A fool.
mnemonic.reading: "BAKA!" A word you've probably heard in anime. (ばか)

examples.ja: そんな馬鹿なことを言うな。
examples.en: Don't say such stupid things.

items.note: In Tokyo-area speech バカ is the common, fairly mild insult; in Kansai アホ is the mild one and バカ sounds harsh. Usually written in kana or katakana (バカ). The horse-and-deer story is a folk explanation: the kanji were chosen for their sound.

mnemonic.meaning: 一 one + 言 word: just one word.
mnemonic.reading: HITO (one) + KOTO (word, like 言葉): one word. (ひとこと)

examples.ja: 最後に一言お願いします。
examples.en: Please say a few words to finish.

items.note: Note the reading: ひとこと, not いちげん.

mnemonic.meaning: 酒 = 氵 (liquid) + 酉 (wine jar): liquid from a jar. Alcohol.
mnemonic.reading: SAKE: the rice wine you know. (さけ) Careful: 鮭 (salmon) is also さけ.

examples.ja: 父は毎晩少し酒を飲む。
examples.en: My father drinks a little alcohol every night.

items.note: In Japan 酒 means any alcohol; rice wine specifically is 日本酒.

mnemonic.meaning: 違 differ + いない not: it can't be different. It must be so.
mnemonic.reading: CHIGAI (difference) + NAI: "there's no difference, it's surely true." (ちがいない)

examples.ja: 彼はもう家に帰ったに違いない。
examples.en: He must have gone home already.

items.note: Used as 〜に違いない (see the grammar sheet). Strong certainty.

mnemonic.meaning: 飛 fly + 出 out: fly out.
mnemonic.reading: TOBI (jump, like 飛ぶ) + DASU (put out): "TOE-BEE DAS-hing out!" (とびだす)

examples.ja: 子供が道路に飛び出した。
examples.en: A child ran out into the road.

items.note: Also "to stick out" or "to leave suddenly": 家を飛び出す.

mnemonic.meaning: 膝 has 月 (body part): the part of the leg that bends. The knee.
mnemonic.reading: "HEE, ZAH!" you yelp when you bang your knee. (ひざ)

examples.ja: 転んで膝をけがした。
examples.en: I fell and hurt my knee.

items.note: 膝の上 = on someone's lap.

mnemonic.meaning: 伸 = a person getting longer. 伸ばす is you making it longer.
mnemonic.reading: "NO, BAS-ta!" you say, stretching your arms. (のばす)

examples.ja: 髪を伸ばしている。
examples.en: I'm growing my hair out.

items.note: Transitive partner of 伸びる (Level 3). Also 延ばす for postponing.

mnemonic.meaning: 多 many + 少 few: many or few. More or less.
mnemonic.reading: "TA-SHO!" Ta-da, a little show. (たしょう)

examples.ja: 多少高くても、質のいい物を買いたい。
examples.en: I want to buy good-quality things, even if they're a bit expensive.

items.note: A bit formal; 少し is everyday. 多少の = some, a certain amount of.

accept: together with others of the same kind

mnemonic.meaning: 同 same + 士 man: people of the same kind.
mnemonic.reading: DOUSHI: "Dou, Shi(t), we're in the same boat!" (どうし)

examples.ja: 友達同士で旅行に行った。
examples.en: We went on a trip together, as a group of friends.

items.note: Usually after a noun: 恋人同士 (a couple), 日本人同士 (between Japanese people).

mnemonic.meaning: 悔 has 忄 (heart): your heart burns with regret.
mnemonic.reading: "KUYA, SHI!" You kick the wall after losing. (くやしい)

examples.ja: 試合に負けて悔しかった。
examples.en: It was so frustrating to lose the match.

items.note: The feeling of losing or being beaten. 残念 is milder disappointment.

mnemonic.meaning: 抵 resist + 抗 oppose: push back against.
mnemonic.reading: TEIKOU: "TAKE OH!" They take it, but you resist. (ていこう)

examples.ja: 新しいルールに抵抗を感じる人も多い。
examples.en: Many people feel resistance to the new rules.

items.note: Also electrical resistance. 抵抗がある = to feel uneasy about something.

mnemonic.meaning: 引 pull + 張 stretch: pull until it stretches.
mnemonic.reading: HIPPARU: "HIP, PA-RUle!" You pull with your hips. (ひっぱる)

examples.ja: 子供が母親の手を引っ張った。
examples.en: The child tugged at its mother's hand.

items.note: Also "to lead a team": チームを引っ張る.

mnemonic.meaning: 真 truly + 赤 red: truly red.
mnemonic.reading: "MAKKA!" Make a red mark. (まっか) The っ gives it a punch, like 真っ白.

examples.ja: 恥ずかしくて顔が真っ赤になった。
examples.en: My face went bright red with embarrassment.

items.note: 真っ赤な嘘 = a complete lie. 真っ青 (まっさお) = deep blue or pale.

mnemonic.meaning: 中 inside + 身 body: the body inside. What's in it.
mnemonic.reading: NAKA (inside) + MI (body, like 身): what's inside. (なかみ)

examples.ja: 箱の中身は何ですか。
examples.en: What's inside the box?

items.note: Also figurative: 話の中身 (the substance of a talk).

mnemonic.meaning: TONDEMONAI: "TON-s of DEMONs, no!" Something wildly beyond normal.

examples.ja: とんでもない値段の時計だ。
examples.en: That watch has an outrageous price.

items.note: Also a polite reply to thanks: とんでもないです = "not at all".

mnemonic.meaning: 殴 has 殳 (weapon/strike): a hand striking.
mnemonic.reading: "NA, GOOO-RU!" the boxer shouts, punching. (なぐる)

examples.ja: 彼はかっとなって相手を殴った。
examples.en: He lost his temper and punched the other man.

items.note: 叩く (たたく) is a lighter tap or knock. 殴る is a hard hit with a fist.

mnemonic.meaning: 正 correct + 体 body: the correct body, under the disguise.
mnemonic.reading: "SHOW, TAI!" Show me your true self. (しょうたい) 正 is しょう here, not せい.

examples.ja: ついに犯人の正体が分かった。
examples.en: At last we found out who the culprit really was.

items.note: 正体不明 = unknown identity.

mnemonic.meaning: 穏 has 禾 (grain) and 心 (heart): a heart at peace, like a calm field of grain.
mnemonic.reading: "ODA! YA-KA!" The calm captain ODA speaks quietly. (おだやか)

examples.ja: 今日は海が穏やかだ。
examples.en: The sea is calm today.

items.note: For weather, seas, people and moods. 穏やかな性格 = a gentle nature.

mnemonic.meaning: 驚 has 馬 (horse): a startled horse rearing up. Surprise.
mnemonic.reading: "ODORO-KI!" Your door opens and you're surprised. (おどろき)

examples.ja: 彼の合格は大きな驚きだった。
examples.en: His passing was a big surprise.

items.note: Noun form of 驚く (to be surprised).

mnemonic.meaning: KICHINTO: a KITCHEN kept neat, everything in its place.

examples.ja: 部屋をきちんと片付けなさい。
examples.en: Tidy your room properly.

items.note: Close to ちゃんと, but more about neatness and order.

mnemonic.meaning: 謎 = 言 (words) + 迷 (lost): words that get you lost. A riddle.
mnemonic.reading: "NAZO?" Not so clear, it's a mystery. (なぞ)

examples.ja: その事件は今でも謎のままだ。
examples.en: That incident is still a mystery.

items.note: 謎を解く = to solve a mystery.
